item.title: Booms heard near Saudi Aramco headquarters as Houthi conflict escalates
item.description:
By Timour Azhari and Menna AlaaElDin

RIYADH, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Loud booms were heard on Tuesday night near the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, the world's largest and the backbone of the kingdom's economy, in Dhahran, six sources told Reuters, amid an escalating war between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition.

item.title: Trump says Houthis trying to drive up oil prices ahead of US midterm elections
item.description:
By Jacob Bogage and Nandita Bose

WASHINGTON, Oct 13 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump on Tuesday accused Yemen's Houthi militants of deliberately trying to drive up oil prices ahead of the US midterm elections and warned that he would "never forget" their attacks on Saudi Arabia, amid a widening regional conflict fueled by the US war with Iran.

"The Houthis are behaving very badly," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post, accusing the group of resuming attacks at Iran's behest after a period of relative quiet following US strikes in Yemen last year.

item.title: In Yemen's Taiz, shelling worsens and prices spiral
item.description:
Oct 13 (Reuters) - With their city encircled by Houthi fighters, residents of Taiz say they face intensifying bombardment and dwindling supplies as the Iran-aligned group tightens its grip on surrounding areas.

Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, has emerged as a major theatre of the conflict between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government, after their war was reignited last month by the U.S.-Iran confrontation in the Gulf.

The Houthis cut off a main road from Taiz to Aden last week, leaving government forces encircled.

item.title: Palestinian officials say Israeli army wounds two in Ramallah raid
item.description:
Israeli army fire wounded two Palestinians on Tuesday during a raid in the city of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, according to the Palestinian health ministry.

A hospital in the city received "a young man with a serious gunshot wound to the lower back and a 14-year-old with a live bullet wound to the upper thigh, in addition to numerous cases of suffocation, as a result of the (Israeli army) assault on Ramallah", the ministry said.

item.title: IMF projects Gulf rebound in 2027. Can energy production keep pace?
item.description: Restoring shipping access in the Strait of Hormuz is only part of the recovery, as Gulf producers also need to repair damaged infrastructure to avoid further disruption to production and exports.
